lines.text: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews, setting an annual celebration on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar.
Haman had cast the Pur, meaning the lot, against the Jews, but the king ordered his scheme to fall on his own head.
The days were called Purim, from the word Pur, and the Jews bound themselves to keep them every year.
Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai wrote to confirm Purim, and Mordecai sent letters to all 120 provinces.
King Xerxes imposed tribute on the land, and Mordecai, second only to him, was recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
